newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to follow Chilean success - Dornbusch.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to follow Chilean success - Dornbusch.

text.p: Argentina, spurred by economic refroms, will achieve a broadly based prosperity for its people within five years, much as Chile has done, U.S. economist Rudiger Dornbusch said Tuesday.

"It is a long-distance race and you do not just buy a pair of shoes and say "now I am Maradonna"," the Massachussets Institute of Technology professor told Reuters during a banking conference in Buenos Aires. "It takes time."
Drawing a parallel with Chile, considered modern Latin America's economic success story, he added:

"Argentina has made fantastic progress and I have every confidence that over the next five years Argentina will look increasingly like Chile and that of course means prosperity on a very broadly shared basis," he added.

Asked about some economists' charges that Argentina's insufficiently developed manufacturing sector will hold the country back in coming years, Dornbusch said: "I think you might say the same of Chile."
"I would recommend to look at Chile and reassess whether manufacturing is important to having high growth. Chile has done extremely well in the last 15 years," he said.
"I believe increasingly the restructuring that is taking place (in Argentina) is putting on the scene quite a lot of firms like the Techint group that are very quickly becoming world class."
Additionally, he said politics was having less and less of an influence on the economy in Argentina, where it has always been a major weight on country risk.
"I do not think in Argentina politics is that important to the economy. There is a broad convergence of views, just as in Chile before, about how the economy has to be operated."

Turning to recent suggestions of introducing a common currency for the Mercosur customs union grouping Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay, Dornbusch said: "It's the dollar -- that has to be the answer, anything else would be insane."
He argued that the sooner Latin American countries, mainly Mexico, adopt the dollar as their currency pegs, the better.
"If Mexico does, look for Venezuela and Colombia to come next and there will be a trickle effect and all of it (Latin America) would be in dollars in ten years," said Dornbusch.
Dornbusch made a name for himself when he accurately predicted the 1994 crash of the Mexican peso.
